In mains, we went for the Hainanese chicken rice, and it was spot on. The poached chicken breast was incredibly tender, and the rice—cooked in rich chicken broth and fat—was packed with flavor. It came with a side of fresh salad and a sweet chili dipping sauce.Overall, it was a delightful experience.

Also loved how friendly the staff was. Definitely a spot I’ll be visiting again. Great experience overall!

featured_reviews.name: VlogWithFurkan

We tried their Chicken Chilli Dumplings – perfectly crispy and packed with juicy, spicy filling. The Chicken Spring Rolls were golden and crunchy, absolutely delicious! For drinks, we had the Pineapple Mojito, which was super refreshing, and the Strawberry Milk Tea, which was creamy and full of flavor – a must-try for bubble tea lovers!

In the mains, the Char Kway Teow Chicken had that perfect smoky wok-tossed taste you’d expect from a Singapore hawker stall. And the highlight was definitely the Sambal Chilli Chicken with Rice – spicy, flavorful, and truly comforting.

The ambience is casual yet vibrant, and the service was great too.
Highly recommended for anyone looking to explore unique Asian flavors in the heart of Mumbai! 🌟

featured_reviews.name: Vivek Vetal
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Persian Darbar in Byculla after hearing a lot of buzz around it. Given its reputation and the constant crowd outside, my expectations were naturally quite high. However, my overall experience was somewhat mixed.

To start with the positives — the ambience is genuinely good. The interiors are well done, with a spacious seating layout and a proper family-restaurant vibe. It feels grand and lively, which explains the heavy footfall. Do note that the place is almost always crowded. If you’re planning to visit, I would strongly recommend booking a table in advance or reaching a little early to avoid the long waiting time.

Coming to the food — I tried the Moroccan Kebab, Murgh Lebnani, Murgh Zafrani Tikka, Bihari Boti, and Chicken Biryani. Honestly, I found most of the dishes average. The taste and quality were mediocre, nothing extraordinary— the kind of flavour you can easily find at many other restaurants on the same street. Given the hype around the place, I expected something more distinctive or memorable. The Moroccan Kebab and Murgh variants were okay, but they didn’t stand out in terms of spice balance or uniqueness. The Bihari Boti was a bit undercooked.

The Chicken Biryani was comparatively better than the rest — flavorful, well-cooked rice, and properly spiced. It was the highlight of the meal for me.

Service, however, was quite slow — probably because of the constant rush. Staff were polite, but you’ll need some patience.

Overall, I felt the place is slightly overhyped. If you’re a hardcore foodie looking for exceptional flavours, you can skip it. If you do visit, go with limited expectations about the taste and focus more on the ambience and overall experience rather than culinary excellence.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Dear Kunal Vijayakar Sir,
I have been following your YouTube channel regularly and often visit places based on your recommendations.
However, I would like to bring to your attention a very disappointing experience I had at Jilani Food Corner, located in Bhori Mohalla, Bhendi Bazaar.
I visited on 5th April 2026 and ordered a parcel of Bheja Masala priced at ₹750. The quantity provided was extremely small, packed in what appeared to be a 250 ml container, which is not justified for the price charged. Additionally, I purchased Chicken Tikka for ₹350, but it consisted of only 4 small shredded pieces, seemingly arranged to give an impression of a larger portion.
Surprisingly, such high prices are not even charged by reputed establishments like Shalimar Restaurant or Delhi Darbar, which offer proper dining facilities including air-conditioned seating and better service.
What made the experience worse was the behavior of the staff. I tried contacting them multiple times regarding my concern, but they either disconnected the calls or did not respond properly. Their attitude was unprofessional and dismissive.
As a loyal viewer, I request you to kindly review such places more carefully. While you may receive good service during visits, regular customers like us may not be treated the same way. It would be helpful if your reviews also highlight aspects like staff behavior, pricing fairness, and portion sizes, in addition to food quality.
I sincerely hope you take this feedback into consideration and avoid promoting such establishments in the future.

featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited KOKO, Lower Parel, on a completely last-minute plan. Their lunch service goes on till 4:00 pm, with the last order taken at 3:15 pm. Luckily, we managed to reach just in time at 3:10 pm.

We ordered the KOKO Signature Roll (avocado, tempura asparagus, crisps, and KOKO sauce) along with Hong Kong Soy Noodles with chicken.

The sushi was the absolute highlight for me – crisp, fresh, and packed with layers of flavour. Every bite was a delight, and it’s definitely something I would love to come back for. The noodles, on the other hand, had a very balanced and subtle taste, making it a nice complement to the meal.

Overall, it was a great experience. The service was quick even though we ordered at the last moment, and the food quality was impressive. Good going, KOKO – I sincerely hope they continue maintaining these high standards!

featured_reviews.review_text: Where do i begin! Best meal i had in mumbai was at KOKO. The mushroom turnip cake, baby potatoes, signature sushi, the noodles , thai lemonade absolutely fire - 10/10. featured_reviews.name: Dr. Minal Kabra
featured_reviews.review_text:
KOKO, Lower Parel – A Luxe Asian Dining Experience

KOKO in Lower Parel offers a refined and memorable dining experience. The ambiance is top-notch — modern, elegant, and perfect for an evening out. The menu features an impressive variety of sushi and dim sum, with ample vegetarian choices that are just as flavorful and thoughtfully prepared as the non-vegetarian options.

The staff is courteous and attentive, adding to the overall premium feel of the place. However, a heads-up for first-timers — they don’t usually offer tables without a reservation, even if some appear to be vacant. Be prepared to sit at the bar if you walk in without prior booking.

That said, once you’re seated, the food and experience are absolutely worth it. For anyone who appreciates quality Asian cuisine in a sophisticated setting, KOKO is highly recommended — just make sure to reserve in advance!

Ordered Chicken Khepsa Rice which was salty as hell, after addressing this issue to the waiter he brought more plain rice which was salty too. Unfortunately had to pack it up due to all the menace. Atleast they gave 10% discount for their mistake that was the only good thing.

featured_reviews.name: Rahul Sohandani
featured_reviews.review_text: Located at 5 minute walking distance from Dockyard station. The kepsa here is an absolute delite. A full kepsa is enough for 4-5 people. Ambience is okay. Service is good and fast. The cost is reasonable.

featured_reviews.name: Shailesh Ayer
featured_reviews.review_text: Worst experience ever. Chicken was partially cooked and was re- fried. Chicken tandoori became so hard due to re over heating. Staff was also not that coprative. I would not sugggest to go there. Instead will suggest to go to Afzal restaurant near by. Much better and good price and taste.
